claims.text: The unusual stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by residual internal stresses generated by thermal-expansion mismatch during solidification and processing.
Conventionally cast, cold-rolled, and aged HfNbTaTiZr has a composite-like microstructure with inherent thermal-expansion-mismatch residual stresses.
Extended isothermal annealing can relax residual thermal stresses without significantly altering phase constitution or grain structure.
Differential thermal contraction among regions during solidification generates heterogeneous residual stresses.
Residual heterogeneous stresses bias the nucleation and evolution of dislocation networks and lattice distortions.
Residual stress and its associated defect networks enhance work hardening during cold rolling.
Residual stress modifies the effective elastic moduli and their temperature dependence.
Residual stress modifies the activation energy for high-temperature dislocation creep.
Samples retaining residual thermal stresses will have greater microhardness after cold rolling than stress-relaxed samples.
Samples retaining residual thermal stresses will show a more pronounced elastic-modulus temperature dependence from 293 to 1100 K than stress-relaxed samples.
Samples retaining residual thermal stresses will have better tensile-creep resistance near 1250 °C than stress-relaxed samples.
Stress-relief annealing will reduce the cold-rolling, thermoelastic, and creep anomalies relative to the conventionally processed baseline.
Microstructure and phase constitution affect the mechanical response of alloys in the HfNbTaTiZr system.
Temperature-dependent elastic anisotropy and elastic moduli occur in a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.

The proposed residual-stress mechanism unifies the previously observed cold-rolling hardening, aging-induced hardening, elastic-modulus temperature dependence, and high-temperature creep behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Intrinsic lattice distortion and compositional heterogeneity may also contribute to the observed behavior.

If verified residual-stress relaxation produces no corresponding change in modulus-temperature dependence, creep resistance, or cold-rolling microhardness, the proposed governing mechanism is falsified.
